audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Azariah/Uzziah, northern coups, Tiphsah atrocity, Assyrian tribute and deportation, and Jotham narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for adolescent accession, chronic skin disease and separate residence, delegated governance, repeated assassinations, Tiphsah massacre including pregnant women, imperial tribute extracted from wealthy people, palace coup, Tiglath-pileser deportations, and escalating Aram-Israel pressure on Judah.

verses.restored: In twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.

familiar.text: In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign.

modern.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה בֶן אֲמַצְיָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Sixteen years old was he when he became king, and fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.

modern.text: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

original.text: בֶּן שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְכָלְיָ֖הוּ מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, according to all Amaziah his father had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done;

modern.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Only high places were not removed; people were still sacrificing and burning incense at high places.

familiar.text: Save that the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burnt incense still on the high places.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there.

original.text: רַ֥ק הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת

verses.restored: YHWH struck king, and he had a skin disease until day of his death and lived in a separate house. Jotham king's son was over house, judging people of land.

familiar.text: And the LORD smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house. And Jotham the king’s son was over the house, judging the people of the land.

modern.text: And the LORD afflicted the king with leprosy until the day he died, so that he lived in a separate house while his son Jotham had charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

original.text: וַיְנַגַּ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה אֶת הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיְהִ֤י מְצֹרָע֙ עַד י֣וֹם מֹת֔וֹ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּבֵ֣ית הַחָפְשִׁ֑ית וְיוֹתָ֤ם בֶּן הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת שֹׁפֵ֖ט אֶת עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ

familiar.text: And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

familiar.text: So Azariah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Azariah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in the City of David. And his son Jotham reigned in his place. Zechariah Reigns in Israel

modern.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah’s reign over Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria six months.

familiar.text: And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.

modern.text: Then Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against Zechariah, struck him down and killed him in front of the people, and reigned in his place.

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Zechariah, they are indeed written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

familiar.text: This was the word of the LORD which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.

modern.text: So the word of the LORD spoken to Jehu was fulfilled: “Four generations of your sons will sit on the throne of Israel.” Shallum Reigns in Israel

verses.restored: Shallum son of Jabesh became king in thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah and reigned one full month in Samaria.

familiar.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.

modern.text: In the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah’s reign over Judah, Shallum son of Jabesh became king, and he reigned in Samaria one full month.

original.text: שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְעֻזִיָּ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ יֶֽרַח יָמִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן

familiar.text: For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.

modern.text: Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down and killed Shallum son of Jabesh, and reigned in his place.

modern.text: At that time Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacked Tiphsah and everyone in its vicinity, because they would not open their gates. So he attacked Tiphsah and ripped open all the pregnant women. Menahem Reigns in Israel

translation_notes: The Hebrew term for Azariah's condition is tsara'at, a broad ritual/skin-disease category, not an automatic diagnosis of Hansen's disease. Translation must avoid the stigmatizing blanket term 'leper.'

Azariah lives separately while Jotham governs. Disability or chronic illness does not erase personhood, moral agency, family bonds, or political identity, and isolation should not be romanticized as proper care.
The northern throne passes through repeated public and palace assassinations. Brief reigns and coup success are not evidence of legitimacy.
Menahem's attack on Tiphsah and ripping open pregnant women are war crimes and reproductive violence. They must be named without graphic sensationalism or ethnic generalization.
Pregnant people and unborn children are not symbols in a royal contest; their bodies expose the extremity of state terror against a city that resisted entry.
Menahem taxes wealthy Israelites to buy Assyrian support for his throne. The payment may prevent occupation temporarily while turning public wealth into regime security.

Assyrian deportation removes entire communities from Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and Naphtali. Exile is coercive population transfer, not a clean geopolitical change.
The chapter's regnal synchronisms are complex and require historical-textual audit; apparent arithmetic tensions should not be silently harmonized.
Mothers' names remain part of Judah's royal record and should not be treated as blame markers for sons' actions.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease or disability, glorify coups, sanitize the Tiphsah atrocity, blame victims of reproductive violence, or treat deportation as ordinary administration. Center bodily dignity, pregnant people's humanity, civilian protection, and the cost of using taxation and empire to secure a throne.
